questions.q: What does a differential backup actually capture?
options: Every transaction since the last log backup
Every page of the database, regardless of when it last changed
Every page changed since the last full backup — not since the last differential
Every page changed since the last differential backup
questions.explain: A differential backup is always relative to the last full backup, which is exactly why it keeps growing through the week until the next full resets it.

questions.q: Why isn't a full backup alone (restored nightly) good enough for Overlook's database?
options: Because a full backup doesn't include the Patients table
Because Azure SQL Database doesn't allow full backups to be restored
Because appointments and billing entries happen throughout the day, so restoring only last night's full could throw away many hours of real activity
Because full backups can only be taken once per month
questions.explain: A full backup alone only gets you back to however the database looked when that backup ran — any activity after that point is lost without differential and log backups to fill the gap.

questions.q: Why does the lesson reject running full backups every hour, even though it would technically work?
options: A full backup copies every page every time, which is slow and wastes storage for only a few hours of real new data each time
Hourly full backups would corrupt the transaction log
Azure SQL Database limits you to one full backup per week by policy
Full backups cannot be scheduled more than once per day in T-SQL
questions.explain: A full backup redoes a complete copy of every page regardless of how little changed, which makes frequent full backups wasteful compared to smaller, faster differential and log backups.

questions.q: In Overlook's planned schedule (weekly full, daily differential, log every 15 minutes during business hours), what does the 15-minute log interval set?
options: The recovery point objective (RPO) — the maximum acceptable data loss
The number of days backups are retained
The total backup storage budget for the month
The recovery time objective (RTO) — how long a restore is allowed to take
questions.explain: A 15-minute log backup interval means, worst case, up to 15 minutes of data could be lost in an outage — that's the RPO the schedule is designed around.

questions.q: To restore Overlook's database to 2:35pm on a Wednesday (full backups run Sunday, differentials run daily), what's the correct restore chain?
options: Sunday's full backup, then the most recent differential (Wednesday's), then every log backup in order up through 2:35pm
Every differential backup taken since Sunday, applied in order
Wednesday's differential backup alone, with no full or log backups needed
Only the most recent log backup before 2:35pm
questions.explain: The restore chain is always full, then the latest differential taken after that full, then every log backup in order from immediately after that differential through the target time.
